title.narrative: IFC Access to Finance phase II
IFC Access to Finance phase II

description.narrative:
Access to Finance fas 2 bygger på framgångar och lärdomar från projektets första fas, som fokuserade på att öka tillgången till finansiering för underfinansierade grupper. Programmet har ett särskilt fokus på små och medelstora företag samt aktörer i Jordbruksvärdekedjan, speciellt kvinnor och kvinnoägda företag, dvs ”de underrepresenterade grupperna”. Programmet bygger vidare på det grundläggande arbetet som har lagts på att åtgärda hinder på utbudssidan (finanssektorn) och på efterfrågesidan (realsektorn). På utbudssidan genom rådgivning och aktiviteter som policyreform, produktutveckling, kapacitetsutveckling av bankerna och innovation kring digital finansiell teknologi. På efterfrågesidan (realsektorn) genom att stärka kompetenser hos låntagare och utvecklingen av kapitalmarknaden.
Programmet har 5 komponenter:
1)Financial Infrastructure
2)Agri supply chain and access to finance
3)MSME banking advisory support
4)Ethiopia capital markets development
5)Environmental, Social and Governance ESG
Programmet avser att genomföra strukturella förändringar och därmed bidra till en hållbar och inkluderande utveckling för tillgång till finansiering. Tillgång till finansiering förväntas leda till utökade ekonomiska möjligheter, ökad produktivitet, ökade arbetstillfällen och i slutändan ha en positiv inverkan på den privata sektorn och på ekonomin i stort.

The Access to Finance Component Phase 2 builds on the successes and learnings from Access to Finance Component Phase 1 Program to increase access to finance for under financed actors, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and agri-value chain actors, with particular focus on smallholder farmers (SHFs), women and youth. The program aims to leverage the foundational work that has been undertaken to address both supply side (financial sector) and demand side (real sector) constraints. Supply side primarily though advisory service for activities such as product development, financer capacitation and financial technology innovation. Demand side (real sector) constraints through borrower literacy, (SMEs) and and capital market development.
The program has five pillars:
1)Financial Infrastructure
2)Agri supply chain and access to finance
3)MSME banking advisory support
4)Ethiopia capital markets development
5)Environmental, Social and Governance ESG
The program seeks to effect structural change and thereby sustainable and inclusive impact on access to finance leading to the expansion of economic opportunities, increased processing capabilities, increased jobs, private sector growth and ultimately impact on the economy at large.

The MDI Access to Finance Phase second phase of the program aims to increase access to finance and thereby economic opportunities for the private sector at large with special focus on small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs); agri-value chain actors ranging from producers, producer organizations to agro-processors (with special focus on women and youth) and women owned businesses i.e. the underserved. The program seeks to effect structural change and thereby sustainable impact on access to finance leading to the expansion of economic opportunities, increased processing capabilities, increases jobs and ultimately impact on the economy at large.
In particular, the program aims to:
*Strengthen and increase financial institutions utilization of the credit information system to enhance the creditworthiness of borrowers and promote the use of their credit histories as collateral complements and substitutes, thus reducing loan collateralization levels.
*Strengthen and increase financial institutions utilization of the MPSR and WRS as tools that would allow them to expand the range of bankable collateral to include movable assets like equipment, purchase orders, accounts receivable, livestock, and commodities, as they are more widely available to marginalized actors and women.
*Leverage digital financial solutions to overcome gaps in bank branch footprints and inefficiencies in loan administration processes.
*Provide hands-on support to financial institutions, including the provision of market analyses, risk appraisals, product design, process enhancement, and go-to-market strategies to boost their understanding and improve their perceptions of opportunities and risks in lending to the underserved via new inclusive financial products and technologies.
*Create and deliver structured financial literacy programs to marginalized actors, including SMEs and agri-value chain actors, with a particular focus on women, in target industries and value chains.
In addition, IFC will lay the foundation for good environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices in the financial and agribusiness sectors to enable a more diversified and resilient economy, and stronger and more sustainable local businesses, which boosts investments.

sector.narrative: Education/training in banking and financial services

description.narrative:
Some of the activities and results are summerised from the programs first year are summerised below with the focus on pre-implementation period
Credit Registry
A bid to procure a new credit bureau system has been put on hold for budget reasons. A new legal framework to regulate credit information sharing was approved by parliament under the amended NBE establishment proclamation. The project team was requested by NBE to make and share recommendations on the new proclamation. Progress in this sector was slow due to withrdrawel of the bid and the need to revised the TOR. The national ID enrollement of microfinance is taking longer than expected.
Commodity Collateralized Financing
The project focused on supporting the Ethiopian Commodities Exchange (ECX)-WRS program to scale up its Warehouse Receipt System (WRS) and expand its reach to farmers. This involved technical assistance, legal framework clarification, and capacity building. A draft collaboration agreement between IFC and ECX is expected to be signed soon. Additionally, the Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA) approved US$300,000 in funding to support the regulatory body's functions.
The Commodity Collateral Financing (CCFII) project facilitated the disbursement of ETB 485.2 million in loans via the three CCF products against 337,923 quintals of maize and wheat; supported the submission of new loan applications totaling ETB 4.4 billion, (34 MUSD ) of which ETB 852.3 million has been approved; and provided extensive technical assistance to Dashen bank to develop the first ever Sharia compliant version of the warehouse receipt financing product. This product has now been approved and is currently being piloted with a select group of farmers seeking ethical financing solutions aligned with their religious values.
Ethiopia Moveable Asset-Based Lending Market Development
The project prioritized livestock-related movable asset-based lending (MABL) initiatives, collaborating with agricultural research organizations and private actors in dairy farming and livestock breeding.The Ministry of Agriculture agreed to support livestock tagging for sheep, goats, and cattle, facilitating the MABL pilot. Training sessions were conducted for financial institutions' staff on the Ethiopian Movable Collateral Registry (EMCR), with 84 participants from 78 financial institutions. Data validation on the collateral registry was performed, identifying gaps for improvement. A diagnostics study on secondary markets was conducted to understand challenges in disposing of defaulted movable assets and to recommend solutions. A diagnostics study on secondary markets was conducted to understand challenges in disposing of defaulted movable assets and to recommend solutions.
Under the movable asset-based lending project, Cooperative Bank of Oromia in collaboration with the project team is developing a financial product for livestock-collateralized loans. The pilot is expected to launch in the upcoming quarter.
Ethiopia Smallholder Supply Chain & Agri-Finance Development/ Green Agro Solutions
Malt Barley Pilot by Lersha: Lersha is a digital platform designed to support smallholder farmers in Ethiopia. It provides a comprehensive range of services, including access to farm inputs, mechanization services, credit, and insurance. Since its launch in 2018, 202,107 farmers have been registered on the Lersha platform. The pilot with Lersha began in July 2024 in 10 kebeles across four woredas in Oromia region. 166 smallholder farmers received seeds, fertilizer, and chemicals, with loans disbursed by Dashen Bank. Parallel pilots in wheat and soybean value chains were initiated in Sidama and Amhara regions, respectively. The pilot facilitated access to finance for 529 farmers across malt barley, wheat, and soybean value chains. Early results indicated an average productivity increase of up to 0.5 tons for most farmers. A scale-up plan was developed to reach 10,000 farmers in Oromia and Sidama regions. IFC will help carry out a detailed review of lessons learned and develop a protype for scale-up
While the malt barley value chain pilot has been successful so far, the number of farmers that were onboarded reached by input financing was limited due to bank documentation issues. Due to the conflict that erupted between opposition groups in the Amhara Region and the federal government and given that Amhara is the largest producer of oil seed crops like soya bean in the country, the circumstances mandated IFC to consider different agri-value chains such as barley or potatoes.
Potato Pilot by Kifiya:The pilot faced delays due to regional government priorities and was relocated to the Gurage zone. 142 farmers were onboarded, with plans to cover 200 hectares and up to 400 farmers. Agreements were signed with banks, PepsiCo, and cooperatives for input supply. The initiative aims to enhance productivity and financial inclusion for smallholder farmers in the potato value chain.
The financial model for the malt barley value chain was finalized, and work on the broader financial model for Green Agro Solutions PLC is in progress.
The agent promotion and communication plan was developed to support the scale-up of Lershas services.
Ethiopia Capital Market Development Project
The Ethiopia Capital Market Development Project achieved significant progress in enhancing the local currency bond market. The project finalized and shared the local currency bond market diagnostic and action plan with key stakeholders, including the Ministry of Finance, the National Bank of Ethiopia, and the Ethiopian Capital Market Authority. A workshop was conducted to discuss and agree on priority actions for implementing the plan.
In terms of legal and regulatory advancements, the project completed and shared the draft Guideline on Corporate Governance for Issuers of Securities to the Public with the Ethiopian Capital Market Authority. The 'Directive on Public Offering and Trading of Securities' was enacted, incorporating corporate governance provisions. Additionally, the development of a non-government bond market framework was initiated.
The inaugural Ethiopia Capital Market Summit was successfully organized, facilitating knowledge sharing and discussions on capital market development. The summit saw the launch of the 'Sustainability Guidelines for Banks in Ethiopia,' enhancing the focus on sustainability in the banking sector. These activities collectively aim to provide better access to long-term local currency finance and support the overall economic development of Ethiopia.
Dashen MSME Banking Advisory
A recently approved project to strengthen Dashen Bank's capacity to serve MSMEs commenced implementation by training bank staff on the MSME-customer value proposition, credit scorecard development, and operational risk. IFC also reviewed the banks MSME credit framework, credit risk appetite criteria, credit processes, and collections and recovery processes, and shared a revised segmentation proposal based on a simplified approach.
Ethiopia Integrated ESG: Financial Institutions
During the reporting period, Dashen Bank's ESG frameworks, including its ESG policy, environmental and social management system (ESMS), exclusion list, and risk rating tool, were developed and approved. IFC provided ESG training for the board of directors and conducted a two-day training-of-trainers workshop for 20 consultants on the Ethiopian Sustainability Guidelines.
Ethiopia Integrated ESG: Manufacturing, Agriculture, and Services
The project managed delays due to leadership changes within the Accounting and Auditing Board of Ethiopia (AABE) and presented a revised draft of the Corporate Governance Directive. A working group was established to develop key documents, and ESG guidelines for the manufacturing and agribusiness sectors were drafted. Additionally, a two-day corporate governance training of trainers was delivered to 28 local consultants, aiming to enhance corporate governance practices in Ethiopian businesses.
